newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syrian army chief slams Netanyahu, warns of war.
newsitem.headline: Syrian army chief slams Netanyahu, warns of war.

text.p: Syria's army chief of staff in remarks published on Thursday condemned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's policies and warned of their "dangerous consequences" on the Middle East peace process.

"The provocation and defiance acts which Netanyahu's government commits daily against Arabs creates an atmosphere that is full of tension," Major-General Hikmat Shihabi told the ruling party newspaper al-Baath.

"Netanyahu's government is playing with fire and its insistence on this aggressive, racist and foolish policy keeps all doors of the region open before the worst and most dangerous consequences," he added.
He said Syria wanted peace that would return the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967, and warned Israel against starting a war with Syria.

"If Netanyahu and his group are working to create war conditions, then Syria is not afraid of war because it is ready for it and knows how to defend itself and its people, and how to protect its national and Arab interests," he said.
"Israel will pay a heavy price if it trod into a foolish aggression against Syria," he added.

"When a single inch of our land remains under occupation that means burning coal is still under the ashes and a remaining mine that is liable to explode at any time will still lead in every second to armed struggle," he said.
Sporadic Syrian-Israeli peace talks faced a new deadlock when Netanyahu ruled out the possibilty of withdrawal from the Golan in return for peace with Syria.
Shihabi, who had taken part in peace talks between Syria and Israel in the United States, did not mention Wednesday's suicide bombing in Jerusalem which killed 13 people.
